nodes.title: Note: MiniMax H3
widgets_values:
## MiniMax H3

[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward. Output is up to 2K resolution, 24fps, and up to about 15 seconds.

## ComfyUI links
- [ComfyUI#15224](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15224)
- [🤗 Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

## About this workflow

This template runs the **reference-to-video (ref2va)** task using the `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo` node. It takes any mix of reference images, videos, and standalone audio, and weaves them into the generation to lock in a character's identity, a style, a motion, a camera move, or a voice.

**Key inputs**

- **ref_images / ref_videos / ref_video_audios / ref_audios**: up to 9 reference images, 3 reference videos (each may carry its own paired soundtrack), and 3 standalone reference audio clips
- **prompt**: reference the inputs by tag, in the exact order they were connected, for example `<Picture 1>`, `<Video 1>`, `<Audio 1>`, then describe the target scene, motion, and audio
- **ref_image_size**: `match` scales references down to the generation's resolution (faster); `max` keeps up to a 2048px short edge for stronger identity fidelity, at the cost of speed since reference tokens ride along every sampling step
- **width / height**: set via Resolution Selector.
- **duration (seconds)**: converted to a valid frame `length` by the Math Expression node

**Sampling and decode**

- Sampler: `res_multistep`. `beta` or `normal` scheduler tends to outperform `simple` for reference-heavy prompts like this one
- The sampler's joint audio+video `LATENT` output feeds directly into both `VAEDecode` (video, `minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16`) and `VAEDecodeAudio` (audio, `minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32`); each decode node automatically pulls its own half out of the packed latent. `CreateVideo` then muxes the two into a single MP4 with synced sound
- The diffusion model here is `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors`, a different set of weights from the `fl2va` model used by the t2v/i2v templates

Ref2va's output is very sensitive to prompt wording; matching the reference tags precisely and being explicit about which reference drives which part of the shot tends to work best.

nodes.title: Note: MiniMax H3 -> LTX-2.5 Refine Pipeline
widgets_values:
## MiniMax H3 -> LTX-2.5 Fast Refine (2-stage pipeline)

**Stage 1 (left side of graph, unchanged):** MiniMax H3 ref2va generates the base clip at 1344x768 with native synced audio, using your reference images/prompt exactly as before. Its own SaveVideo (id 92) still saves this as a low-res preview so you can A/B compare.

**Stage 2 (this new block):** the decoded MiniMax frames are re-encoded into LTX-2.5's own VAE (VAEEncode, node 211) -- this bridge step is required because MiniMax H3 and LTX-2.5 use incompatible latent spaces, so you can't feed one model's latent directly into the other. From there it follows LTX-2.5's real pipeline: LTXVLatentUpsampler (node 212, native x2 spatial upscale) -> a short, LOW-DENOISE SamplerCustomAdvanced pass (nodes 215-219, sigmas 0.35->0.0, only 3 steps) that just adds fine detail/sharpness without redrawing the shot -> VAEDecodeTiled -> muxed with MiniMax's ORIGINAL audio (no need to touch LTX's audio path).

**Result:** MiniMax's 1344x768 -> 2x upscale -> 2688x1536, above 1080p, in a handful of fast LTX-2.5 distilled steps instead of a full slow MiniMax pass at higher res.

**Things to verify once you load this in ComfyUI (I built this from the two workflow JSONs, but couldn't execute it to confirm node compatibility):**
- VAEEncode encoding a full frame sequence into LTX's video VAE should work the same way LTX's own i2v workflow builds video latents, but double-check frame count/temporal alignment on first run.
- LTXVEmptyLatentAudio (silent placeholder) just gives the joint AV sampler the shape it expects -- its audio output is discarded after sampling; only MiniMax's real audio makes it into the final video.
- video_cfg is set slightly higher (1.5) than LTX's own default (1.0) to help the refine pass hold onto MiniMax's exact detail rather than drift -- tune down if it looks over-contrasted, up if it looks too soft.
- If output resolution is too heavy/slow, you can skip LTXVLatentUpsampler and wire VAEEncode's output straight to LTXVConcatAVLatent for a same-resolution detail-only pass.

nodes.title: Note: Custom Resolution Mode
widgets_values:
## Resolution Mode Switch (nodes 250-255)

Toggle **node 250** (Boolean):
- **True (default): Custom Target Resolution.** MiniMax's decoded frames get resized in pixel space (node 253, lanczos, no fixed ratio) to whatever width/height you set in nodes 251/252 -- e.g. 1920x1080, 1280x720, 1080x1920, or any arbitrary size -- then re-encoded into LTX's VAE and refined. This is the path to use since you want exact target resolutions, not just a fixed 2x multiplier.
- **False: Native x2 Upscaler Model.** Falls back to the original fixed-ratio LTXVLatentUpsampler path (nodes 211/212) -- MiniMax's resolution x2, whatever that comes out to. Slightly higher native quality per-pixel since it's a learned latent upscaler rather than a pixel resize, but you can't pick an exact target size with it.

Either path feeds into the same refine denoise pass (nodes 214-223) with the sigma/cfg settings from before -- so all the sharpness/identity tuning still applies regardless of which resolution mode you pick.

Note: the custom-resolution path resizes BEFORE re-encoding into LTX's latent space, so it's not upscaling an already-encoded latent -- it's a clean resize on the actual pixels, which is why arbitrary aspect ratios/sizes work reliably here (a model-based upscaler like node 212 is trained for one fixed ratio only).

nodes.title: Input Text (Prompt)
widgets_values:
subject_definitions:

<Subject 1> is the young woman shown in <Picture 1>, with black hair tied in a high ponytail with bangs, pale skin, dark eyes, a white cropped tank top, black leather shorts, black thigh-high boots, black arm guards, and a red-and-black utility belt and holster. She is holding a black handgun. Preserve her exact facial identity, hairstyle, clothing, accessories, body proportions, handgun, and realistic photographic appearance throughout the video.

<Picture 1> is the single visual reference image for <Subject 1>, defining her appearance, starting pose, indoor environment, lighting, wardrobe, weapon, and overall visual style.


summary:

[reference generation] The target video shows <Subject 1> in a fast cinematic action sequence. She starts from the crouched position shown in <Picture 1>, reacts to an off-screen threat, quickly turns and raises her handgun, fires toward the unseen threat, moves to nearby cover, and finishes in a strong aiming stance. The action is fast, controlled, and physically believable.


retention_analysis:

<Subject 1> (appears throughout [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - her facial identity, ponytail, outfit, accessories, handgun, proportions, and overall appearance remain consistent with <Picture 1>.

<Picture 1> ([Shot 1] starting reference): fully_preserved - the character appearance, starting pose, environment, lighting, and overall visual design are retained.


detailed_description:

The target video is a fast realistic action scene based on <Picture 1>. The indoor environment remains consistent with the reference, with the same lighting and overall appearance.

[Shot 1] The video begins from <Picture 1>. <Subject 1> remains crouched low for a brief moment, holding the handgun with both hands. She suddenly looks toward something off-screen and her expression changes from focused to alert.

She quickly turns her upper body toward the direction of the threat and raises the handgun into a ready position.

<Subject 1> then fires several controlled shots toward the off-screen threat. Small brief muzzle flashes appear at the handgun with each shot. Her arms react naturally to the recoil and she maintains a stable stance.

Immediately afterward, she lowers her center of gravity and quickly moves sideways toward nearby cover. Her movement is fast and purposeful, with natural body mechanics.

She reaches cover, briefly leans behind it, then quickly rises back into view and aims the handgun toward the same off-screen direction.

The final moment shows <Subject 1> in a strong crouched aiming stance, eyes focused and alert, handgun held firmly with both hands.

Keep the action fast and continuous. The progression is:

crouched → notices threat → turns → raises handgun → controlled firing → moves to cover → aims again.

Do not add unnecessary acrobatics, flips, or complicated choreography. Keep the action grounded and easy to follow.

The camera follows her movement with energetic handheld motion, including a quick lateral movement during the transition to cover. Keep <Subject 1> clearly visible and maintain her face and body proportions.

The handgun remains consistently shaped and positioned in her hands. Recoil should be subtle and physically believable.

Do not show any visible injuries, blood, or graphic impact. The threat remains off-screen.

Preserve the exact character identity, hairstyle, clothing, weapon, environment, and lighting from <Picture 1>.

overall_soundscape:

Indoor ambience, rapid footsteps, clothing movement, brief handgun reports, subtle recoil sounds, and movement against the nearby cover.

non_diegetic_music:

A fast tense action soundtrack with a strong rhythmic pulse plays throughout the sequence.

Note: Manual Sigmas Value Tips
widgets_values:
Faithfull to original refine pass: 0.35, 0.22, 0.12, 0.0

Middle Ground: 0.7, 0.55, 0.3, 0.0

LTX-2.5's own high-res refine pass: 0.85, 0.7250, 0.4219, 0.0


Heads up on the tradeoff: a deeper sigma range means the sampler has more freedom, so there's a slightly higher chance of subtle drift from MiniMax's exact face/outfit than before. If that happens, drop video_cfg back to ~1.5–1.7 first before touching the sigmas — that's the more surgical knob. If it's still not sharp enough even at 0.85 start, the next lever is adding a step (e.g. 0.9, 0.75, 0.55, 0.3, 0.0) rather than raising cfg further, since more cfg past a point just adds contrast/artifacts rather than real detail.

Faithfull to original refine pass: 0.35, 0.22, 0.12, 0.0

Middle Ground: 0.7, 0.55, 0.3, 0.0

LTX-2.5's own high-res refine pass: 0.85, 0.7250, 0.4219, 0.0


Heads up on the tradeoff: a deeper sigma range means the sampler has more freedom, so there's a slightly higher chance of subtle drift from MiniMax's exact face/outfit than before. If that happens, drop video_cfg back to ~1.5–1.7 first before touching the sigmas — that's the more surgical knob. If it's still not sharp enough even at 0.85 start, the next lever is adding a step (e.g. 0.9, 0.75, 0.55, 0.3, 0.0) rather than raising cfg further, since more cfg past a point just adds contrast/artifacts rather than real detail.
